text:
Sports Illustrated ran the headline this week: "How Filip Forsberg Broke out of his Slump and Saved Nashville's Season." The Predators have won six straight, and Forsberg has 14 points in his last ten games, including both goals in Tuesday's 3-0 win in Los Angeles behind a Juuse Saros shutout. He has 22 points in 19 games and plenty of shots behind them (48).

Here's the part to keep in mind. With Forsberg on the ice, Nashville has scored 13.4 more goals than its chances deserve, and on-ice luck like that fades. At five-on-five the Predators are slightly behind on chances with him out there (49% of expected goals). His own shooting is fine: seven goals on 6.5 expected, so the finishing isn't the issue. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him as a player whose chances deserved far more than he got (2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual). This year the bounces are paying him back with interest. The shot volume is real; the scoring pace leans on teammates' pucks going in.
headline: Forsberg's hot run is real volume, borrowed luck
